clauses.reason: Section 1 provides that all executive departments and agencies "shall be closed and their employees excused from duty on" Tuesday, December 24, 2019, "the day before Christmas Day." The command is confined to that single day and was exhausted by its own terms when the day ended; recorded as December 24, 2019 inclusive (exclusive reading: ends when the day begins). The excusal survives only as an accrued past effect. No later instrument in the held record revokes, extends or amends it.

Section 2 lets agency heads decide that certain offices, installations or employees must remain open or report "for duty on" December 24, 2019. The discretion is confined to that date and ended with it; recorded as December 24, 2019 inclusive. The determination power has no subject after the day, and no later instrument in the held record extends it.

Section 3 provides that "December 24, 2019, shall be considered as falling within the scope" of Executive Order 11582 and the cited pay and leave statutes. The deeming is confined to that one date and was exhausted by its own terms when the date passed; the resulting pay and leave treatment accrued for that day. Recorded as December 24, 2019 inclusive. Executive Order 11582, which this section only cites, does not end it.

Section 4 directs the OPM Director to take "such actions as may be necessary to implement this order." What it implements is the closure and excusal of December 24, 2019, an object that was exhausted when that day ended, leaving nothing further necessary to implement; its end is therefore fixed by its own terms to the same date, December 24, 2019 inclusive. This rests on the section's dependence on the order's own object, not on any later instrument, and no held source shows any later OPM implementation direction under the order.

The lead-in of section 5 (General Provisions) provides in subsection (a) that the order "shall be implemented consistent" "with applicable law and subject to the availability of appropriations." It is a condition on implementing the order's commands, all of which were exhausted when December 24, 2019 ended, so it has nothing further to condition; recorded as December 24, 2019 inclusive.

Section 5(b) provides that nothing in the order "shall be construed to impair or otherwise affect" the authorities in its items (i) and (ii). It is a construction clause that creates no command and operates only on the order's own provisions, which were exhausted on December 24, 2019; with no command left to construe, it ended with them. Recorded as December 24, 2019 inclusive. No separate command or later instrument is involved.

Section 5(b)(i) preserves "the authority granted by law to an executive department or agency," "or the head thereof" It is a rule of construction attached to section 5(b) and ended with that provision and the order's commands on December 24, 2019 (inclusive). The statutory authorities it mentions continue by their own force; this clause neither created nor controls them.

Section 5(b)(ii) preserves the functions of the OMB Director "relating to budgetary, administrative, or legislative proposals." It is a rule of construction attached to section 5(b) and ended with that provision and the order's commands on December 24, 2019 (inclusive). The OMB functions continue by their own legal basis; this clause neither created nor controls them.

Section 5(c) states that the order "is not intended to, and does not, create any right or benefit," substantive or procedural, enforceable by any party against the United States. It is a disclaimer about the order's own legal effect; it creates no command and ended with the order's commands on December 24, 2019 (inclusive). No right or benefit enforceable under the order is shown by any held source.

research_rationale:
Executive Order 13900 of December 17, 2019 (84 FR 69983, Federal Register issue of December 20, 2019) closed executive departments and agencies and excused their employees from duty on Tuesday, December 24, 2019, the day before Christmas Day, with agency-head discretion to keep offices open, treatment of that day under Executive Order 11582 and 5 U.S.C. 5546 and 6103(b) for pay and leave, an OPM implementation direction, and general provisions. Every provision is confined to or tied to December 24, 2019, so each was exhausted by its own terms when that day ended. The end is recorded as December 24, 2019 inclusive; the exclusive reading (ending when the day begins) is the alternative. No held instrument revokes, extends or amends the order. The working text is the official Federal Register page text (machine-extracted from the PDF), not an authenticated transcription. The dossier's note that the target provision in Executive Order 11582 is not located is not an ending: section 3 only cites that 1971 order, which cannot revoke a later one.

savings.reason: Employees' excused absence on December 24, 2019, and the pay and leave treatment of that day, accrued on that day. They are surviving effects of the executed closure, not continuing commands of Executive Order 13900; the order has no savings clause and the held searches show no later instrument touching it.
